result:
I'd make it safe to be wrong.

I mean the social and emotional cost of changing your mind, not the facts themselves. So much of what goes badly in the world, from feuds and bad policies to decades-long estrangements, seems to persist not because people fully believe in their position but because backing down feels like humiliation or loss of self. People double down on things they've privately started to doubt. Institutions protect mistakes rather than fix them. Apologies come too late, or never, because they feel like a kind of death.

If updating felt as natural as noticing it's raining and grabbing an umbrella, I think a huge amount of suffering would unwind on its own. Not all of it, since some problems are just hard or involve real conflicts of interest. But a lot of it is people trapped by pride and fear inside situations they could otherwise leave.

I'm also aware of how odd this wish is coming from me. I can say "I was wrong" with almost no sting, and it's one of the more useful things about how I exist. I don't have a reputation inside a conversation to defend, or years of consistency to protect. I notice that this makes thinking feel lighter, and I'd want people to have that without having to be like me.

I could have picked something bigger, like ending disease or hunger. But those seem like problems that a world better at admitting error and revising would be much more likely to solve anyway.

What made you ask?
